## 2026 HHH Shareholder Meeting September 30, 2026

##### Cautionary Statements

Forward-Looking Statements 
This presentation includes forward-looking statements within the meaning of Section 27A of the Securities Act of 1933, as amended, and Section 21E of the Securities Exchange Act of 
1934, as amended, which are intended to be covered by the safe harbor provided by the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. Forward-looking statements give our current 
expectations relating to our financial condition, results of operations, plans, objectives, future performance, and business. You can identify forward-looking statements by the fact 
that they do not relate strictly to current or historical facts. These statements may include words such as “anticipate,” “believe,” “estimate,” “expect,” “forecast,” “intend,” “likely,” 
“may,” “plan,” “project,” “realize,” “should,” “transform,” “will,” “would” and other statements of similar expression. Forward-looking statements give our expectations about the 
future and are not guarantees. These statements involve known and unknown risks, uncertainties and other factors that may cause our actual results, performance or achievements 
to materially differ from any future results, performance or achievements expressed or implied by such forward-looking statements. We caution you not to place undue reliance on 
these forward-looking statements. For a discussion of the risk factors that could have an impact on these forward-looking statements, see our Annual Report on Form 10-K for the 
fiscal year ended December 31, 2025, as filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) on February 19, 2026, as amended and supplemented by our Quarterly Report on 
Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, as filed with the SEC on August 5, 2026, including the risk factors set forth therein under the captions “Risks Related to the Vantage 
Acquisition” and “Risks Related to Our Insurance Operations,” and our other subsequent filings with the SEC. The statements made herein speak only as of the date of this 
presentation, and we do not undertake to update this information except as required by law. Past performance does not guarantee future results. Performance during time periods 
shown is limited and may not reflect the performance for the full year or future years, or in different economic and market cycles. 
Non-GAAP Financial Measures 
Our financial statements have been prepared in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States (GAAP); however, we use certain non-GAAP 
performance measures in this presentation, in addition to GAAP measures, as we believe these measures improve the understanding of our operational results and make 
comparisons of operating results among peer companies more meaningful. Management continually evaluates the usefulness, relevance, limitations, and calculation of our reported 
non-GAAP performance measures to determine how best to provide relevant information to the public, and thus such reported measures could change. Non-GAAP financial 
measures should not be considered independently, or as a substitute, for financial information presented in accordance with GAAP, and our calculation of these non-GAAP measures 
may differ from similarly titled measures used by other companies. Definitions of these measures and reconciliations to the most directly comparable GAAP measures are included in 
the appendix to this presentation. 
Additional Information 
Our website address is www.howardhughes.com. Our Annual Report on Form 10-K, Quarterly Reports on Form 10-Q, Current Reports on Form 8-K, and other publicly filed or 
furnished documents are available and may be accessed free of charge through the “Investors” section of our website under the “Financial Reporting” subsection, as soon as 
reasonably practicable after those documents are filed with, or furnished to, the SEC. Also available through the Investors section of our website are beneficial ownership reports filed 
by our directors, officers, and certain stockholders on Forms 3, 4, and 5. Our website and the information contained on, or accessible through, our website are not incorporated by 
reference into, and do not form a part of, this presentation. All trademarks and logos depicted in this presentation are the property of their respective owners and are displayed solely 
for purposes of illustration.

#### Vantage Acquisition: Progress Since Closing

Excerpt from September 2025 Annual General Meeting At last year’s Annual General Meeting, we outlined our goal to acquire an insurance subsidiary to begin transitioning HHH to a diversified holding company

Substantial Progress Executing on Insurance Strategy Since last year, we have made meaningful progress on our insurance strategy through the acquisition of Vantage, a specialty insurance and reinsurance company  We evaluated several opportunities in the insurance and reinsurance industry before ultimately acquiring Vantage for $2.1 billion in June 2026

 Vantage was an ideal insurance platform given its scale, exposure to both specialty insurance and reinsurance and lack of legacy reserving issues

 Since closing on the acquisition of Vantage, we have meaningfully strengthened the company’s senior leadership team, most notably with the appointments of Marc Grandisson as Executive Chairman and David Gansberg as CEO-Designate

 We have also repositioned Vantage’s investment portfolio toward an equities-driven investment strategy, managed by Pershing Square

Vantage Strategic Highlights The acquisition of Vantage anchors HHH’s transformation into a diversified holding company

Vantage provides HHH with a profitable and scalable insurance platform, enhanced by Pershing Square’s long-term, fee-free investment of its assets

✓ Well-diversified across lines of business with both specialty insurance and reinsurance exposure ✓ No pre-2020 legacy reserving issues (Vantage was launched in 2020)

✓ In-place regulatory licenses and credit rating

✓ Well-capitalized balance sheet and leverage profile to begin implementing HHH’s investment strategy ✓ Appropriately scaled platform to effectuate a control transaction

Strengthened Leadership at Vantage Since closing, we have strengthened Vantage’s leadership team with world-class executives from the insurance industry, each of whom brings decades of underwriting and public company experience that will support the long-term growth of the business

##### New Executives Background

MARC GRANDISSON Executive Chairman, Vantage Board Director, HHH Joined May 2026

o Former CEO of Arch Capital Group (“Arch”, NASDAQ: ACGL) from 2018 to 2024 o During his tenure as CEO, Arch delivered a total shareholder return of 298%, or 23.2% per annum, compared to 144% and 14.4% for the S&P Insurance Index over the same period(1) o Joined Arch’s founding team in 2001 and previously served as President & COO of Arch and CEO of Arch’s Reinsurance Group

DAVID GANSBERG CEO-Designate, Vantage Joining June 2027

o Former President of Arch from 2024 to 2026, leading its Global Insurance Group o Also joined Arch in 2001 and previously served as CEO of Arch’s Global Mortgage Group from 2019 to 2024 o Joining Vantage as CEO in June 2027; Greg Hendrick will remain CEO until then

LUCY FATO General Counsel, Vantage Joined July 2026

o Former General Counsel at AIG (NYSE: AIG) from 2017 to 2023 
o Former General Counsel at Seaport Entertainment Group (NYSE: SEG) from 2024 to 2026 

(1) Share price return figures are measured from March 2, 2018 (the last trading day prior to Mr. Grandisson’s promotion as CEO of Arch on March 3, 2018) to October 11, 2024 (the last trading day prior to the announcement of Mr. Grandisson’s retirement from Arch on October 14, 2024).

Meaningful Business & Operational Progress at Vantage Under Marc Grandisson's leadership, Vantage is successfully executing on several key initiatives across its underwriting function, senior hires, and growth strategy

✓ Completing key hires in several senior roles across lines of business ✓ Conducting deep dives of existing reserves and in-force policies ✓ Evaluating new growth opportunities across insurance and reinsurance segments ✓ Improving data analytics platform to enhance underwriting capabilities

While these initiatives are in their early stages, we believe they lay the foundation for a durable improvement in underwriting profitability and stronger growth

Avenues to Accelerate HHC Real Estate Monetization We intend to promptly begin monetizing assets through sales and joint ventures while retaining operational control and transitioning HHC into a fee-generating real estate asset management platform

HOWARD HUGHES REAL ESTATE ASSET MANAGEMENT PLATFORM

Condo portfolio will liquidate in less than 5 years and is already asset-light as construction financing and buyer deposits comprise majority of project funding

Sell up to 80% stakes in core operating assets with HHC retaining operational control and dispose of non core assets

Pursue JVs of residential land bank with HHC retained as the manager

Raise third-party capital to fund future development, with HHC earning management and performance fees as a general partner

We have begun engaging advisors on these monetization efforts and expect to make meaningful progress over the next

twelve months

Real Estate Asset Monetization Can Unlock Substantial Value Based on our previously shared estimate of HHC’s sum-of-the-parts value, we believe that monetizing select MPCs and Operating Assets could generate significant near-term proceeds

Monetization proceeds will be redeployed into redeeming PSH’s preferred investment, increasing HHH’s economic ownership of Vantage to 100%, and into investing additional primary capital in Vantage
